extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents and attorneys), USPTO OED staff, and parties to USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order / settlement agreement setting out stipulated misconduct (communication violations), legal conclusions under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, and the specific sanctions, duties, and procedural requirements imposed on a patent practitioner (agent) by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline and the USPTO Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2) — reasonable consultation with client
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished (example: not consulting with the client as to why three provisional patent applications were filed for the same invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page cites the respondent's failure to explain why three provisional applications were filed as the factual basis for this violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — keeping client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter (examples: telling the client inaccurate filing dates; not informing the client that two provisional applications were filed on January 2, 2018 and that a third was filed on January 17, 2018; not providing filing receipts; not providing copies of the provisional applications; not using alternate means of communication when primary means were inaccessible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document lists numerous specific failures to inform the client (incorrect representations about filing dates, failure to provide receipts and copies, failure to use alternate contact methods while an assigned email was inaccessible) as illustrative conduct that violates § 11.104(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b) — explaining matters to permit informed decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation (examples: not informing the client that a third party, PLUSA, was paying the practitioner and not disclosing the amount; not explaining why three provisional patent applications were filed or whether filing three separate applications was advisable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order uses the practitioner's omissions about third-party payment and the rationale for multiple filings as the basis for finding a violation of § 11.104(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: 30-day suspension from practice before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent matters for thirty (30) days, which shall commence fourteen (14) days after the date that the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension commencement and duration are explicitly specified; other duties/responsibilities during suspension are set out elsewhere in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24-month probationary period
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month probationary period commencing on the signing of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation begins immediately on signing and lasts 24 months; special enforcement procedures apply if respondent fails to comply during probation (see Order to Show Cause provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on engaging in practice of patent matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not engage in the practice of patent matters as defined by 37 C.F.R. § 11.5(b)(1) during the suspension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an absolute bar for the suspension term and until reinstatement as defined elsewhere in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain suspended until petition for reinstatement is granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the USPTO until the OED Director grants Respondent's petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even after the 30-day suspension term, reinstatement is required under § 11.60 for resumption of practice if specified conditions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPRE requirement within 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent, at his own expense within twelve (12) months from the signing of the Final Order, shall take the Multi-State Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE), attaining a score of 85 or better, and provide a declaration to the OED Director with accompanying corroborating documents verifying compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must submit documentary proof corroborating the MPRE score/attainment along with a declaration; the requirement must be satisfied within the 12-month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: CLE requirements within 12 months on legal ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must successfully complete three Continuing Legal Education (CLE) classes on legal ethics where the primary subject matters are (i) communication with clients; (ii) trust accounts and safe keeping property; and (iii) law practice management; and provide corroborating proof of successful completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborating proof includes documentary evidence of attendance and completion, a description of the course content for which credit was received, and a copy of all written materials provided to course participants (or other corroborating proof acceptable to the OED Director).

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Agreement, Final Order, or USPTO Rules during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not immediately suspend the Respondent for up to an additional sixty (60) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order to Show Cause shall be sent to Respondent's last address of record; Respondent is granted fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director may request additional suspension up to 60 days
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after consideration of Respondent's response (if any), the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver the Order to Show Cause, Respondent's response (if any), and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request that the USPTO Director enter an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to an additional sixty (60) days for the violations set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the documented escalation path for alleged noncompliance during probation and may result in an immediate additional suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may seek further discipline under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19–11.57
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order shall prevent the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 through 11.57 for any misconduct engaged in by Respondent prior to, during, or after his probationary period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order does not limit the Office's ability to pursue separate or additional disciplinary action; prior or subsequent misconduct may be considered as aggravating in future proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60 except as expressly addressed by the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order incorporates the duties and petition-for-reinstatement rules from §§ 11.58 and 11.60 and modifies or specifies which parts apply or are deferred (see subsequent entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 — notice to clients and arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide notice of his suspension to all clients he represents having immediate or prospective business before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(ii), and shall make appropriate arrangements for legal services to be rendered on behalf of his clients during the period of his suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must conform to the requirements of § 11.58(b)(1)(ii); respondent must arrange continuity of client representation as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 — notice to opposing practitioners/parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide notice of his suspension to the practitioners for all opposing parties (or to the parties in the absence of a practitioner representing the parties) in matters pending before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty ensures other parties or their counsel in pending matters receive timely notification of the practitioner's suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 — not holding out as authorized to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not hold himself out as authorized to practice before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(3) until he is reinstated to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must cease representations (signage, advertising implying ability to practice before the USPTO) that suggest authorization while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 — no legal advice or services
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not render legal advice or services to any person having immediate or prospective business before the Office as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(5) until he is reinstated to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits all legal activity before the Office on behalf of others while suspended, even informal advice regarding Office matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions respondent does NOT have to comply with unless petition not granted within 90 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not have to comply with certain duties as a consequence of being suspended unless a petition for reinstatement is not granted within 90 days of the Final Order. These include: (1) filing a notice of withdrawal in each pending application (§ 11.58(b)(1)(i)); (2) delivering to all clients documents (§ 11.58(b)(1)(iv)); (3) relinquishing client or fiduciary funds and unearned fees (§ 11.58(b)(1)(v)); (4) removing telephone, legal or other directory advertisement/statements (§ 11.58(b)(1)(vi)); (5) changing existing advertising regarding availability or ability to perform services for persons with business before the Office (§ 11.58(b)(4)); and (6) changing signs/stationery to delete representations suggesting authorization to practice (§ 11.58(b)(1)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit temporary exceptions tied to an administrable 90‑day period after entry of the Final Order; if petition remains unresolved after 90 days, the listed duties may become mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of compliance under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide an affidavit of compliance certifying that he has complied with the provisions of the Agreement and the Final Order. Appended to the affidavit shall be a copy of each form of notice, the names and addresses of the clients, practitioners, courts, and agencies to which notices were sent, and all return receipts or returned mail received up to the date of the affidavit as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit must demonstrate compliance and include documentary proof of notices and their recipients; specific contents are set by § 11.58(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit exclusions — items not required to be included
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's affidavit need not include: (1) a schedule showing the location, title and account number of every bank account designated as a client or trust account (§ 11.58(b)(2)(ii)); (2) a schedule describing disposition of client and fiduciary funds in Respondent's possession (§ 11.58(b)(2)(iii)); (3) proof of proper distribution of funds and closing of such accounts including copies of checks (§ 11.58(b)(2)(iv)); or (4) an affidavit describing steps taken to remove advertisements suggesting authorization to practice (§ 11.58(b)(2)(vi)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly lists these categories as not required in the affidavit of compliance appended to the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: No limited recognition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Respondent's suspension shall commence fourteen (14) days after the date that the Final Order is signed, Respondent shall not be granted limited recognition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timing of the suspension's commencement precludes limited recognition under the cited rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 — filing and attestation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not resume practice until reinstated by order of the OED Director or USPTO Director as set forth in § 11.60(a). After the term of suspension and compliance with applicable provisions of § 11.58, Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement as set forth in § 11.60(b). Any petition for reinstatement shall be filed with the OED Director and accompanied by the required fee (§ 11.60(c)). Upon filing, the petition must comply with §§ 11.60(c)(1)–(3) and shall attest to compliance with § 11.58, including a sworn declaration that the respondent has not engaged in the practice of patent matters before the Office during suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must follow the procedural and substantive elements of § 11.60, include the fee, and include sworn attestations of compliance and non-practice during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director need not publish notice of petition for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director does not have to publish a notice of Respondent's petition for reinstatement as set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly waives the OED Director's obligation to publish a notice of the reinstatement petition under the cited subsection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room. The OED Director shall also publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided Notice of Suspension and Probation text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Order will be made public via the OED Reading Room and an Official Gazette notice summarizing the suspension, probation, violations, and remedial requirements will be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural appeals and costs allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives seeking reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, review under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and otherwise appealing or challenging the Final Order in any manner. The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the Agreement and Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By agreeing to the settlement, respondent gives up rights to reconsideration/review/appeal relating to this Final Order; each party bears its own costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in reaching the settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: In reaching this settlement the OED Director considered that Respondent: (1) expressed contrition; (2) recognized the seriousness of his actions; (3) fully cooperated with the USPTO since the filing of the Complaint; and (4) has not been previously disciplined by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mitigating factors are explicitly listed as considerations informing the sanction decision.
